analysis.title: September credit delinquencies improve as originations continue to grow
key_insights: Non-mortgage delinquencies improved y/y in September: 60+ day bankcard 2.74% vs 2.83% a year ago, personal loan 3.26% vs 3.28%, auto 1.50% vs 1.57%. Card and auto remain above their long-term averages since 2009 (2.50% and 1.02%), personal loans below (3.76%).
Lower-tier performance is mixed: subprime and near-prime delinquencies rose in cards and personal loans, while subprime auto improved and near-prime auto was unchanged.

Originations grew y/y in July (latest data): cards +2.7%, personal loans +10.9%, auto +1.3%, mortgage +21.1%. Continued delinquency improvement could support a gradual easing of underwriting standards.

Mortgage 90+ day delinquency rose to 1.01% from 0.73% a year ago but stays well below the 2.47% long-term average. Elevated rates (30-year at 7.2% on Oct 29), limited inventory and high prices constrain affordability.

Consumer backdrop is mixed: unemployment 4.2% in September vs 4.1% in August (below 5.6% average since 1990), real wages -0.7% y/y, savings rate 4.1% vs 5.8% average, household debt 57.8% of GDP and debt service 11.1% of disposable income, both below long-term averages.

Card originations: prime +0.4% and subprime +11.3% y/y in July; card balances +3.3% y/y to $1.2tn. Personal loan originations: prime +7.4%, subprime +17.0%, 18 consecutive months of positive y/y growth, 13 of them double digit.
Auto originations returned to growth (+1.3% y/y in July vs -0.9% in June), with prime -0.3% and subprime +9.4%. Comparisons are tougher after a tariff-related pull-forward earlier in 2025.

GS favors Buy-rated FICO for pricing power, entrenched position in credit decisioning and robust EPS growth, supported by the Mortgage Direct License Program (DLP) and Software transformation. Risks: FHFA unified mortgage pricing grid, broader VantageScore availability and possible bi-merge adoption.

FICO: mortgage origination revenue +97% y/y in F3Q after +127% in F2Q, now 62% of Scores revenue. DLP agreements cover ~73% of reseller volume, potentially ~90% if another large reseller signs. Platform ARR growth accelerated to 62% y/y from 49%, and Platform ARR now exceeds non-Platform ARR for the first time.

EFX (Neutral, $169 PT): EWS Verifier diversified revenue +13% y/y in 3Q. Government is a 2027 catalyst, with substantially all of $150mn new state ACV expected to contribute in 2027. VantageScore is used by ~2,000 lenders, volumes up >230% since April. Run rates imply a high-single-digit decline in 2027 mortgage market transactions, and bi-merge exposure is ~$80mn annual revenue before mitigation.

TRU (Neutral, $78 PT): revenue ex-mortgage growing ~5.5% y/y, auto +13%. Mortgage inquiries fell 16% y/y in 3Q and are expected to fall more than 20% in 4Q, slowing OCC revenue growth ex-FICO royalties to 3-5% from ~5.5%. A full shift to bi-merge would cut annual revenue ~$33mn and EPS $0.15 before mitigation. 2026 underlying margin expansion outlook cut to flat to 20 bps, and higher interest expense is a ~$60mn headwind in 2027.

market_movers.rationale: Pricing power, entrenched position in credit decisioning, DLP rollout and Software transformation support double-digit EPS growth. Regulatory and competitive uncertainty warrants a lower multiple. PT cut to $961 from $1,129 (Oct 2).
Diversified EWS growth and government and AI upside are balanced by mortgage pressure and bi-merge revenue exposure of ~$80mn. PT raised to $169 from $148 (Oct 2).
Resilient non-mortgage growth and Insurance momentum are offset by declining mortgage volumes, lower margin expansion and higher interest expense. PT raised to $78 from $68 (Oct 2).

sector_views.rationale: GS favors business models with pricing power, leading positions, recurring revenue and idiosyncratic catalysts amid uneven consumer credit and mortgage regulatory uncertainty. FICO is Buy, EFX and TRU Neutral.
Non-mortgage delinquencies improved y/y and originations are growing, but lower-tier performance is mixed and real wages are falling.

earnings_insights: FICO F3Q (reported, quarter ended Jun-26): mortgage origination revenue +97% y/y, after +127% in F2Q. Platform ARR growth 62% y/y vs 49% prior quarter.

EFX 3Q (reported): EWS Verifier diversified revenue growth 13% y/y. Company outlook for 100 bps of ex-FICO EBITDA margin expansion and a $150mn multi-year AI productivity goal, despite an $80mn mortgage revenue shortfall vs prior outlook.

TRU 3Q (reported): revenue ex-mortgage growth ~5.5% y/y, auto +13%, mortgage inquiries -16% y/y. 4Q company guide: mortgage inquiries down more than 20% y/y, OCC revenue growth ex-FICO royalties 3-5%.

GS estimates: FICO FY2026E (Sept-26E year) adjusted EPS $43.01, FY2027E $48.64. EFX 2026E adjusted EPS $8.53, 2027E $10.06. TRU 2026E adjusted EPS $4.87, 2027E $5.55. These are GS forecasts, not reported figures.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Down from 2.83% a year ago and up from 2.71% in August, still above the 2.50% long-term average.
Down from 3.28% a year ago, below the 3.76% long-term average.
Down from 1.57% a year ago and up from 1.32% in August, well above the 1.02% long-term average.
Up from 0.73% a year ago, well below the 2.47% long-term average. Limited risk of a broad wave of defaults.

Indicates modest pressure on consumer purchasing power.
Elevated, constraining housing affordability and purchase activity.

risk_factors: FICO: inability to sustain elevated Scores price increases, competitive threats, macro and credit downturn, lack of traction in decision management software.
FICO mortgage economics: FHFA unified mortgage pricing grid, broader VantageScore availability, possible bi-merge transition reducing mortgage score volumes.

EFX downside: macro and rate risk, subprime credit origination headwinds, mortgage origination volume volatility. Upside: mortgage rebound, non-mortgage inquiry expansion, EWS adoption, international growth.

TRU downside: macro and credit downturn, mortgage origination declines, M&A dilution, FX headwinds, financial leverage. Upside: stronger economy, international and emerging markets growth, US emerging verticals.
Consumer: falling real wages, low savings rate, rising unemployment, elevated mortgage rates and home prices.

tension_points.bull_case: Mortgage origination revenue +97% y/y in F3Q, DLP covering ~73% of reseller volume, pricing flexibility, and Platform ARR growth of 62% support robust revenue growth and double-digit EPS growth.
tension_points.bear_case: FHFA's unified mortgage pricing grid, broader VantageScore availability and a possible transition to bi-merge create market share and volume risk for Classic FICO.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A shift to bi-merge or an FHFA pricing grid that reduces FICO mortgage score volumes or pricing, or DLP coverage failing to reach the second large reseller.

tension_points.bull_case: Non-mortgage delinquencies improved y/y, originations are growing, and household leverage and debt service are below long-term averages, which could support easing underwriting.
tension_points.bear_case: Real wages fell 0.7% y/y, the savings rate is below average, unemployment rose to 4.2%, and subprime and near-prime delinquencies rose in cards and personal loans.
